strings.item.u1-q1.prompt: It is 9 o'clock in the morning and you meet your neighbor. Which greeting do you say?
strings.item.u1-q1.expl: At 9 in the morning you say Guten Morgen. This greeting is used until about 11 o'clock.
strings.item.u1-q1.dyk: Most German greetings depend on the time of day.
strings.item.u1-q1.hint: Look at the time: it is still morning.
strings.item.u1-q1.opt.b.why: Guten Tag is a common greeting, but it is only used from about 11 o'clock; until then Guten Morgen applies.
strings.item.u1-q1.opt.c.why: Learners often mix up the times of day; Guten Abend is only said from about 6 p.m., and most greetings depend on the time of day.
strings.item.u1-q1.opt.d.why: Gute Nacht means 'good night' and is said when someone is going to sleep, not when meeting someone.
strings.item.u1-q2.prompt: Write the German greeting that is used at 2 p.m.
strings.item.u1-q2.expl: At 2 p.m. you say Guten Tag. This greeting is used from about 11 a.m. to 6 p.m.
strings.item.u1-q2.hint: Noon has already passed, but it is not evening yet.
strings.item.u1-q3.expl: From about 6 p.m. you say Guten Abend, which means 'good evening'.
strings.item.u1-q4.prompt: It is 8 p.m. and you walk into a café. What do you say to the waiter when you arrive?
strings.item.u1-q4.expl: When you arrive at 8 p.m., you say Guten Abend. Gute Nacht is not a greeting for arriving but an expression for going to sleep.
strings.item.u1-q4.hint: You are arriving in the evening, not going to sleep.
strings.item.u1-q4.opt.b.why: Croatian speakers often use 'laku noć' as an evening greeting too, but Gute Nacht is said when someone is going to sleep, not on arrival.
strings.item.u1-q4.opt.c.why: Guten Morgen is only used until about 11 a.m.; at 8 p.m. it is evening.
strings.item.u1-q5.prompt: Sort the expressions: greeting on arrival or expression for going to sleep.
strings.item.u1-q5.expl: Gute Nacht is said when someone is going to sleep. Guten Morgen, Guten Tag and Guten Abend are greetings on arrival.
strings.item.u1-q5.dyk: Guten Abend is used from about 6 p.m.
strings.item.u1-q5.hint: One expression is not used as a greeting when meeting someone.
strings.item.u1-q6.expl: When someone is going to sleep, you say Gute Nacht, which means 'good night'.
strings.item.u1-q6.hint: Imagine you are saying goodbye before bed.
strings.item.u1-q7.prompt: You are talking to an elderly lady you do not know. Which word for formal 'you' do you use?
strings.item.u1-q7.expl: You address an older person you do not know with Sie. It is written with a capital S.
strings.item.u1-q7.dyk: Sie is always written with a capital S.
strings.item.u1-q7.hint: A stranger who is older calls for the polite form.
strings.item.u1-q7.opt.b.why: Du is the informal form for friends, family and children; with an older person you do not know, you use Sie.
strings.item.u1-q7.opt.c.why: Ihr is the form for several people you address with du; it is not used to address a stranger politely, that is Sie.
strings.item.u1-q8.prompt: With which person do you use Sie, and with which du?
strings.item.u1-q8.expl: You use Sie with strangers, in business situations and with older people. You use du with friends, family and children.
strings.item.u1-q8.hint: Ask yourself whether you have a close relationship with the person.
strings.item.u1-q8.entry.e2: a boss at a business meeting
strings.item.u1-q8.entry.e3: an elderly gentleman you do not know
strings.item.u1-q9.expl: When you are not sure, the safest choice is Sie. It is a polite, formal form.
strings.item.u1-q9.hint: It is better to be polite than too familiar.
strings.item.u2-q1.prompt: Conjugate the verb sein in the present tense.
strings.item.u2-q1.expl: The verb sein is highly irregular, just like the English 'to be'. That is why you need to learn the forms by heart: ich bin, du bist, er ist, wir sind, ihr seid.
strings.item.u2-q1.dyk: The form ist is always singular, and sind is always plural.
strings.item.u2-q1.hint: The forms do not resemble one another, just like 'am, are, is' in English.
strings.item.u2-q2.prompt: Which form of the verb sein belongs in the sentence: Wir ___ aus Kroatien. (we)
strings.item.u2-q2.expl: Wir (we) takes the form sind. Sind is always plural, and ist is always singular.
strings.item.u2-q2.opt.b.why: Ist is the singular form (er ist). Wir (we) takes the plural: wir sind.
strings.item.u2-q2.opt.c.why: Seid goes with ihr (you, several people), not with wir. Wir takes sind.
strings.item.u2-q2.opt.d.why: Bin goes only with ich (I). Wir takes sind.
strings.item.u2-q3.prompt: Complete the sentence with a form of the verb sein.
strings.item.u2-q3.expl: With du, the verb sein is bist: du bist. It is not formed like a regular verb, because sein is highly irregular.
strings.item.u2-q4.prompt: Conjugate the verb haben in the present tense.
strings.item.u2-q4.expl: Haben is mostly regular, but irregular in some forms. Remember du hast and er hat; the rest are ich habe, wir haben, ihr habt.
strings.item.u2-q4.hint: Two forms are shorter than the rule would suggest.
strings.item.u2-q5.prompt: Which form of the verb haben belongs in the sentence: Du ___ Zeit. (you)
strings.item.u2-q5.expl: With du, the verb haben is hast: du hast. Haben is irregular in some forms, so you do not say habst.
strings.item.u2-q5.opt.b.why: Haben is partly irregular, so it is not formed like a regular verb: du hast, not habst.
strings.item.u2-q5.opt.c.why: Hat goes with er/sie/es (third person singular). Du takes hast.
strings.item.u2-q5.opt.d.why: Habe goes with ich (I). Du takes hast.
strings.item.u2-q6.prompt: Write the form of the verb haben that goes with er (without the pronoun).
strings.item.u2-q6.expl: With er (he, she, it), the verb haben is hat. It ends in -t, not in -en.
strings.item.u2-q6.hint: Think of the form that is irregular.
strings.item.u2-q7.prompt: Conjugate the regular verb wohnen in the present tense.
strings.item.u2-q7.expl: Wohnen is a regular verb: wohne, wohnst, wohnt, wohnen, wohnt. The polite form Sie wohnen looks like the plural, even though it can refer to one person.
strings.item.u2-q7.dyk: Sie is always written with a capital letter and can mean one person or several.
strings.item.u2-q7.hint: It follows the same pattern as singen: singe, singst, singt.
strings.item.u2-q8.prompt: You politely ask one stranger where they live: Wo ___ Sie?
strings.item.u2-q8.expl: With the polite Sie, the verb ends in -en: Wo wohnen Sie? This holds even when you are asking just one person.
strings.item.u2-q8.hint: Verb forms ending in -en are plural, but Sie is special.
strings.item.u2-q8.opt.b.why: Wohnt goes with er or ihr. The polite Sie always takes the -en form: Wo wohnen Sie?
strings.item.u2-q8.opt.c.why: Wohnst goes with du. When you say Sie, the verb is the same as in the plural: wohnen, even though it is about one person.
strings.item.u2-q8.opt.d.why: Wohne goes with ich (I). Sie takes wohnen.
strings.item.u2-q9.prompt: Complete the sentence with a form of the verb wohnen.
strings.item.u2-q9.expl: With er, the verb wohnen is wohnt: er wohnt. The third person singular ends in -t.
strings.item.u2-q9.hint: Think of the pattern singe, singst, singt.
strings.item.u3-q1.prompt: How do you say the number 11 in German?
strings.item.u3-q1.expl: The number 11 is elf. After it comes zwölf, which is 12.
strings.item.u3-q2.expl: Dreißig is 30. Do not confuse it with dreizehn, which is 13, or with sechzig, which is 60.
strings.item.u3-q2.dyk: The tens are zwanzig, dreißig, vierzig, fünfzig, sechzig, siebzig, achtzig and neunzig.
strings.item.u3-q2.hint: The tens end in -zig, and 30 is spelled dreißig.
strings.item.u3-q2.opt.a.why: Dreizehn is 13 and dreißig is 30: they start similarly, but -zehn means 13, while -ßig marks a ten.
strings.item.u3-q2.opt.c.why: Drei is 3. Dreißig starts with drei, but it is a ten: 30.
strings.item.u3-q3.expl: After zehn (10) and elf (11) comes zwölf (12).
strings.item.u3-q4.prompt: Match the German number with the numeral.
strings.item.u3-q4.expl: Vierzehn is 14, fünfzehn is 15, sechzehn is 16, and siebzehn is 17.
strings.item.u3-q4.hint: The first part of the word is the unit: vier, fünf, sechs, sieben.
strings.item.u3-q5.prompt: How do you say 24 in German?
strings.item.u3-q5.expl: In the number 24, the unit comes first, then und, then the ten: vier + und + zwanzig.
strings.item.u3-q5.dyk: Numbers from 21 to 99 put the unit first.
strings.item.u3-q5.hint: The unit comes before the ten.
strings.item.u3-q5.opt.b.why: The order is not like in English: in German the unit comes first, then und, then the ten.
strings.item.u3-q5.opt.c.why: Between the unit and the ten there is always und: vier-und-zwanzig.
strings.item.u3-q5.opt.d.why: That is 42 (zwei + und + vierzig). For 24 the unit is vier and the ten is zwanzig.
strings.item.u3-q6.prompt: Write the German number 21 as one word.
strings.item.u3-q6.expl: The number 21 is einundzwanzig: ein (one), und (and) and zwanzig (twenty).
strings.item.u3-q6.hint: It starts with the unit and is written as one word.
strings.item.u3-q7.prompt: Which word joins the unit and the ten in the number einundzwanzig?
strings.item.u3-q7.expl: Between the unit and the ten comes und, which means 'and'. That is how ein-und-zwanzig is formed.
strings.item.u3-q8.prompt: In what order are German numbers from 21 to 99 built?
strings.item.u3-q8.expl: Numbers from 21 to 99 are all built the same way: the unit, then und, then the ten. So 24 is vierundzwanzig.
strings.item.u3-q8.back: Unit + und + ten, for example vierundzwanzig (24).
strings.item.u3-q9.prompt: The waiter in a café politely asks you: "Was möchten Sie?" What is he asking you?
strings.item.u3-q9.expl: Was möchten Sie? means 'What would you like?'. This is how the waiter politely asks what you want to order.
strings.item.u3-q9.dyk: Friends would ask: Was möchtest du?
strings.item.u3-q9.hint: The waiter wants to know your order.
strings.item.u3-q9.opt.b.why: How much is that? is Was kostet das? Möchten asks what the guest wants to order.
strings.item.u3-q9.opt.c.why: How are you? is Wie geht es Ihnen? Was möchten Sie? does not ask about your health but about what you would like to order.
strings.item.u3-q9.opt.d.why: What is your name? is Wie heißen Sie? In a café, Was möchten Sie? asks what you would like.
strings.item.u3-q10.expl: The short order is Einen Kaffee, bitte. The word bitte is the polite 'please'.
strings.item.u3-q10.dyk: You can also say: Ich hätte gerne einen Kaffee, bitte.
strings.item.u3-q10.hint: The polite word at the end of an order.
strings.item.u3-q11.prompt: What is the verb möchte used for in a café?
strings.item.u3-q11.expl: The verb möchte is used to say what someone wants to order. An example is the sentence about a colleague who wants a latte macchiato.
strings.item.u3-q11.hint: Think of ordering in a café.
strings.item.u3-q11.back: You say what someone would like to order, for example: meine Kollegin möchte einen Latte Macchiato.
strings.item.u4-q1.prompt: Match the German word with its English meaning.
strings.item.u4-q1.expl: Der Vater is father, die Mutter mother, das Kind child, and der Bruder brother. Learn the article together with the noun.
strings.item.u4-q1.hint: Pay attention to the articles der, die and das.
strings.item.u4-q2.prompt: Write the German word for 'mother' together with the definite article.
strings.item.u4-q2.expl: Mother is die Mutter. The article is part of the word, so learn it together with the noun.
strings.item.u4-q3.expl: Die Eltern means parents, that is, mother and father together. Brothers and sisters are a separate word: die Geschwister.
strings.item.u4-q3.dyk: Grandmother and grandfather are die Großmutter and der Großvater, and informally die Oma and der Opa.
strings.item.u4-q3.opt.b.why: Die Eltern and die Geschwister get mixed up; die Geschwister means brothers and sisters, and die Eltern means parents.
strings.item.u4-q3.opt.c.why: Children are die Kinder; die Eltern are the people who have children, that is, the parents.
strings.item.u4-q3.opt.d.why: Grandmother and grandfather are die Großmutter and der Großvater; die Eltern means mother and father together.
strings.item.u4-q4.prompt: Write the German word for 'sister' together with the definite article.
strings.item.u4-q4.expl: Sister is die Schwester, feminine. Brother is der Bruder.
strings.item.u4-q5.prompt: Which definite article does a neuter noun have in the nominative singular?
strings.item.u4-q5.expl: You recognize the gender by the article in the nominative singular: der for masculine, die for feminine and das for neuter. An example of a neuter noun is das Bild.
strings.item.u4-q5.hint: Three genders, three articles; neuter is neither der nor die.
strings.item.u4-q5.opt.b.why: Der is the masculine article (der Berg); neuter has das (das Bild).
strings.item.u4-q5.opt.c.why: Die is the feminine article (die Kraft) and the plural article; neuter has das.
strings.item.u4-q6.prompt: Sort the nouns by the article they take in the singular.
strings.item.u4-q6.expl: Der Berg and der Vater are masculine, die Kraft and die Mutter feminine, and das Bild and das Kind neuter. Learn the article together with the noun.
strings.item.u4-q6.dyk: The letter ß is called Eszett or scharfes S and stands for a double s, as in the word Großmutter.
strings.item.u4-q6.hint: Father is masculine and mother is feminine.
strings.item.u4-q7.prompt: How many genders do German nouns have?
strings.item.u4-q7.expl: German nouns have three genders: masculine, feminine and neuter. Each gender has its own article in the singular: der, die and das.
strings.item.u4-q7.hint: Look at how many singular articles there are.
strings.item.u4-q7.opt.b.why: German, like Croatian, has three genders. Besides masculine and feminine there is also neuter, with the article das (das Kind).
strings.item.u4-q7.opt.c.why: Every German noun has a gender. You can see the gender from the article der, die or das.
strings.item.u4-q8.prompt: Which article goes with the plural 'Kinder' (children)?
strings.item.u4-q8.expl: In the plural the definite article is always die, for all three genders. The singular is das Kind and the plural is die Kinder.
strings.item.u4-q8.hint: In the plural, gender no longer makes a difference.
strings.item.u4-q8.opt.b.why: Das is the neuter singular article (das Kind); in the plural the article is always die.
strings.item.u4-q8.opt.c.why: Der is the masculine singular article (der Vater); in the plural all genders take the article die.
strings.item.u4-q9.expl: Der Vater is masculine and die Mutter is feminine. Learn the article together with the noun.
strings.item.u4-q9.hint: Father is masculine and mother is feminine.
strings.item.u4-q10.prompt: Write the definite article before the word Eltern (parents, plural).
strings.item.u4-q10.expl: Die Eltern is plural, and in the plural the article is always die. This holds for all three genders.
strings.item.u4-q10.hint: The word means more than one person.
strings.item.rp-u1-1.prompt: Frau Weber is a receptionist you do not know. How do you ask her how she is?
strings.item.rp-u1-1.expl: With someone you do not know at work, the formal Sie is used, so the question is Wie geht es Ihnen?
strings.item.rp-u1-1.opt.b.why: Dir is the informal form (du) for friends and family, and Frau Weber is a person you do not know.
strings.item.rp-u1-1.opt.c.why: This question means what is your name, informally with du; it does not ask how someone is.
strings.item.rp-u1-2.prompt: The next morning at 8 o'clock you see Frau Weber again. Write the German greeting for that time of day.
strings.item.rp-u1-2.expl: Guten Morgen is said in the morning, until about 11 o'clock.
strings.item.rp-u2-1.prompt: Write in German: I live in Zagreb.
strings.item.rp-u2-1.expl: The verb wohnen is regular: with ich it takes the ending -e, so you say Ich wohne in Zagreb.
strings.item.rp-u2-2.prompt: Pablo asks whether you have time today. Complete the answer: Ja, ich ___ heute Zeit.
strings.item.rp-u2-2.expl: With ich, the verb haben is habe: ich habe.
strings.item.rp-u2-2.opt.b.why: Hast is the form for du (you), and here you are talking about yourself, ich.
strings.item.rp-u2-2.opt.c.why: Hat is the form for er, sie and es (he, she, it), not for ich.
strings.item.rp-u2-2.opt.d.why: Haben is the infinitive and the form for wir, sie and Sie, not for ich.
strings.item.rp-u2-3.prompt: Pablo asks where you come from. How do you answer?
strings.item.rp-u2-3.expl: Kommen is a regular verb like wohnen: with ich it takes the ending -e, so you say Ich komme aus Kroatien.
strings.item.rp-u2-3.opt.b.why: The ending -st goes with du (du kommst); with ich the verb ends in -e.
strings.item.rp-u2-3.opt.c.why: The verb sein is not needed in this sentence: one verb is enough, ich komme.
strings.item.rp-u3-1.prompt: You want to know how much a piece of cake costs. What do you ask the waiter?
strings.item.rp-u3-1.expl: Was kostet das? means How much is that? and this is how you ask the price.
strings.item.rp-u3-1.opt.b.why: This question is asked by the waiter: it means What would you like?, and it does not ask the price.
strings.item.rp-u3-1.opt.c.why: This question means What is your name?, and it does not ask the price.
strings.item.rp-u3-2.prompt: Politely order a piece of cake.
strings.item.rp-u3-2.expl: With ich möchte and bitte the order is polite: Ich möchte ein Stück Kuchen, bitte.
strings.item.rp-u3-2.opt.b.why: Danke means thank you; when you ask for something, the polite word is bitte.
strings.item.rp-u3-2.opt.c.why: That is the waiter's question to a guest (Would you like a piece of cake?), not your order.
strings.item.rp-u4-1.prompt: Mia asks whether you have any brothers or sisters. Write in German: Yes, I have a sister.
strings.item.rp-u4-1.expl: Sister is die Schwester, feminine, so you say eine Schwester: Ja, ich habe eine Schwester.
strings.item.rp-u4-2.prompt: Your parents live in Split. How do you tell Mia?
strings.item.rp-u4-2.expl: Eltern is always plural, so you say meine Eltern with a plural verb: Meine Eltern wohnen in Split.
strings.item.rp-u4-2.opt.b.why: Eltern is plural, and with a plural noun the possessive is meine, not mein.
strings.item.rp-u4-2.opt.c.why: Wohnt is the form for er, sie, es or ihr; with a plural (sie, die Eltern) the verb is wohnen.
strings.art.a-u1-1.title: Greetings and Forms of Address: du or Sie
strings.art.a-u1-1.body:
Most German greetings depend on the time of day [1]. So first look at the time: until about 11 o'clock you say Guten Morgen (good morning) [2], from about 11 until about 6 p.m. you say Guten Tag (good day) [3], and in the evening, from about 6 p.m., you say Guten Abend (good evening) [4].

Gute Nacht (good night) is not a greeting on arrival. It is said when someone is going to sleep [5]. When you arrive at someone's home or at a café in the evening, say Guten Abend, and save Gute Nacht for going to bed [4, 5].

German has two words for 'you': informal du and formal Sie [6]. Sie is always written with a capital S [7].

You use Sie with strangers, in business situations and with older people [8]. You use du with friends, family, children and people your own age once you already know them [9]. The basic rule is: you say Sie to a person you do not have a close relationship with [10].

If you are not sure which form to choose, the safest choice is Sie [11].
strings.art.a-u2-1.title: The Verbs sein, haben and wohnen in the Present Tense
strings.art.a-u2-1.body:
The verb sein (to be) is highly irregular, just like the English verb 'to be' [1]. Its present-tense forms are: ich bin, du bist, er ist, wir sind, ihr seid [2]. The form ist is always singular, and the form sind is always plural [3].

The verb haben (to have) has these present-tense forms: ich habe, du hast, er hat, wir haben, ihr habt [4]. Haben is mostly regular, but irregular in some forms, so it is good to learn it by heart [5].

Regular verbs follow the same pattern as singen: singe, singst, singt, singen, singt [6]. The verb wohnen (to live, to reside) is conjugated regularly [7] and belongs to the A1 level vocabulary [8]. For the third person singular you say er wohnt [9].

In the plural we have wir wohnen and sie wohnen, and the polite form is Sie wohnen [10]. Verb forms ending in -en are plural, even though the polite Sie can refer to one person [11]. Sie is always written with a capital letter and is used for one person and for several people [12].
strings.art.a-u3-1.title: Numbers and Ordering in a Café
strings.art.a-u3-1.body:
The German numbers from 0 to 20 are the foundation for all other German numbers [1]. So learn them well first. The numbers from 0 to 12 are: null, eins, zwei, drei, vier, fünf, sechs, sieben, acht, neun, zehn, elf and zwölf [2].

The numbers from 13 to 19 are: dreizehn, vierzehn, fünfzehn, sechzehn, siebzehn, achtzehn and neunzehn [3]. The tens are: zwanzig (20), dreißig (30), vierzig (40), fünfzig (50), sechzig (60), siebzig (70), achtzig (80) and neunzig (90) [4].

Numbers from 21 to 99 are built by one rule. The unit comes first, then und ("and"), and finally the ten, so 24 is vierundzwanzig [5]. That is how 21 becomes einundzwanzig: ein (one), und (and) and zwanzig (twenty) [6].

In a German café, the waiter asks the guest what they would like. The polite question is "Was möchten Sie?", and among friends you say "Was möchtest du?" [7]. With the verb möchte you say what someone would like to order [8].

An order can be short: "Einen Kaffee, bitte." [9]. You can also say "Ich hätte gerne einen Kaffee, bitte" or "Ich nehme einen Espresso" [10].
strings.art.a-u4-1.title: Family and the Three Noun Genders
strings.art.a-u4-1.body:
German nouns have three genders: masculine, feminine and neuter [1]. You recognize the gender by the definite article in the nominative singular: der for masculine, die for feminine and das for neuter [2]. Examples are der Berg (masculine), die Kraft (feminine) and das Bild (neuter) [3].

In the plural, the definite article in the nominative is always die, for all three genders [4]. So learn the article together with the noun: do not learn Vater, but der Vater.

The word for family is die Familie [5]. Father, mother and child are der Vater, die Mutter and das Kind [6]. Son, daughter, brother and sister are der Sohn, die Tochter, der Bruder and die Schwester [7].

Die Eltern means parents, and die Geschwister means brothers and sisters [8]. Grandmother and grandfather are die Großmutter and der Großvater, and informally die Oma and der Opa [9]. Der Onkel is uncle, and die Tante is aunt [10].

Notice the letter ß in the word Großmutter. It is called Eszett or scharfes S and stands for a double s [11].

strings.rp.sc.u1-hotel.title: Arriving at the Hotel
strings.rp.sc.u1-hotel.setting: Hotel Linde, 8 p.m. You arrive at the hotel and the receptionist, Frau Weber, welcomes you. Goal: greet according to the time of day and speak formally, with Sie, to someone you do not know.
strings.rp.sc.u1-hotel.l2.help: It is 8 p.m., evening. Greet Frau Weber with the greeting used in the evening.
strings.rp.sc.u1-hotel.l3.tr: I am Frau Weber. Pleased to meet you! Here is your key.
strings.rp.sc.u1-hotel.l4.help: Frau Weber is someone you do not know, at work. Ask her how she is, but formally: with Ihnen, not with dir.
strings.rp.sc.u1-hotel.l5.tr: Thank you, I am well! You must be tired.
strings.rp.sc.u1-hotel.l6.help: You are going to your room to sleep. This is not an arrival greeting like Guten Abend: what do you say when someone is going to sleep?
strings.rp.sc.u1-hotel.l8.tr: (The next morning.) It is eight o'clock. Breakfast is ready!
strings.rp.sc.u1-hotel.l9.help: It is 8 a.m. Write the greeting that is used until about 11 o'clock: Guten ...
strings.rp.sc.u1-hotel.l10.tr: Enjoy your meal! And later: goodbye!
strings.rp.sc.u2-sprachcafe.title: At the Language Café
strings.rp.sc.u2-sprachcafe.setting: Berlin, a language café for people learning German. You meet Pablo from Spain. Goal: say where you come from, where you live and whether you have time to study together.
strings.rp.sc.u2-sprachcafe.l1.tr: Hi! I am Pablo. I come from Spain. I am learning German.
strings.rp.sc.u2-sprachcafe.l2.tr: And you? Where are you from?
strings.rp.sc.u2-sprachcafe.l3.help: Pablo asks where you come from. Answer for yourself: the verb kommen with ich ends in -e, and the country comes after aus.
strings.rp.sc.u2-sprachcafe.l4.tr: From Croatia? Croatia is a beautiful country! And where do you live?
strings.rp.sc.u2-sprachcafe.l5.help: Pablo asks where you live. Start with Ich and the verb wohnen in the form for ich, then add in Zagreb.
strings.rp.sc.u2-sprachcafe.l6.tr: Zagreb is a beautiful city! And your friend Marko? Is he here in Berlin too?
strings.rp.sc.u2-sprachcafe.l7.help: Marko is not in Berlin. Say that he lives in Zagreb: the verb wohnen with er ends in -t.
strings.rp.sc.u2-sprachcafe.l8.tr: Shall we learn German together? Do you have time today?
strings.rp.sc.u2-sprachcafe.l9.help: Pablo asks whether you have time today. Answer for yourself, person ich: the verb haben with ich ends in -e.
strings.rp.sc.u3-cafe.title: At the Café
strings.rp.sc.u3-cafe.setting: A café in Vienna, in the afternoon. The waiter Jonas serves you. Goal: politely order a coffee and a cake, ask the price and pay the bill.
strings.rp.sc.u3-cafe.l1.tr: Good afternoon! We have coffee, tea and cakes. What would you like?
strings.rp.sc.u3-cafe.l2.help: Jonas asks what you would like. Order a coffee and add the polite word that means 'please'.
strings.rp.sc.u3-cafe.l3.tr: With pleasure. And a piece of cake? The cake is very good today.
strings.rp.sc.u3-cafe.l4.help: You want to know how much the cake costs. Ask the question about the price.
strings.rp.sc.u3-cafe.l6.help: Jonas is waiting for your order. Politely say that you would like a piece of cake: Ich möchte ... and at the end the word for 'please'.
strings.rp.sc.u3-cafe.l7.tr: Here you are! Here is your coffee, your cake and water.
strings.rp.sc.u3-cafe.l8.tr: And this is the bill. (The bill says 11 €.)
strings.rp.sc.u3-cafe.l9.help: The bill says 11 €. Say the amount in German: which word means 11?
strings.rp.sc.u4-foto.title: The Family Photo
strings.rp.sc.u4-foto.setting: At your friend Mia's home. Mia shows you a photo of her family. Goal: name the family members with the right article and say something about your own family.
strings.rp.sc.u4-foto.l1.tr: Look! This is my family. Guess: who is this?
strings.rp.sc.u4-foto.l2.help: Mia is pointing at her father and mother. Vater is masculine and Mutter is feminine: which article goes with each word?
strings.rp.sc.u4-foto.l3.tr: Correct! And this is my brother Paul. He is thirty years old.
strings.rp.sc.u4-foto.l4.tr: Do you have any brothers or sisters?
strings.rp.sc.u4-foto.l5.help: Mia asks whether you have any brothers or sisters. Say that you have one sister: start with Ja, ich habe ... and do not forget that Schwester is feminine.
strings.rp.sc.u4-foto.l6.tr: Nice! And your parents? Where do they live?
strings.rp.sc.u4-foto.l7.help: Mia asks where your parents live. Eltern is plural: you need meine and a plural verb.
strings.rp.sc.u4-foto.l8.tr: Great! Paul has two children: Lena and Max.
strings.rp.sc.u4-foto.l9.help: Kinder is the plural of Kind. In the plural all genders have the same article: which one?
strings.rp.sc.u4-foto.l10.tr: Yes, very cute! And here are my grandmother and my grandfather.
strings.rp.sc.finale.title: Mia's Birthday
strings.rp.sc.finale.setting: Berlin, 7 p.m., Mia's birthday party at her home. You meet her brother Paul and his daughter. Goal: greet people, say where you are from and where you live, politely accept a piece of cake and guess how old Mia is.
strings.rp.sc.finale.l2.help: It is 7 p.m., evening. Greet Mia with the evening greeting: Guten ...
strings.rp.sc.finale.l4.tr: Hi! Nice to meet you. Where are you from?
strings.rp.sc.finale.l5.help: Paul asks where you come from. The verb kommen with ich ends in -e, and the country comes after aus.
strings.rp.sc.finale.l6.tr: Great! Do you live here in Berlin?
strings.rp.sc.finale.l7.help: Paul asks whether you live in Berlin. You do not: say that you live in Zagreb, the verb wohnen with ich.
strings.rp.sc.finale.l8.tr: Here is my birthday cake! Would you like a piece?
strings.rp.sc.finale.l9.help: Mia offers you cake. Politely say that you would like a piece: Ich möchte ... and at the end the word for 'please'.
strings.rp.sc.finale.l10.tr: And this is my daughter Lena. She is four years old.
strings.rp.sc.finale.l11.help: Kind is a neuter noun. Which article goes with neuter: der, die or das?
strings.rp.sc.finale.l12.tr: Guess: how old am I today? Twenty plus one!
strings.rp.sc.finale.l13.help: Twenty plus one is 21. In German the unit comes first, then und, then the ten: ein + und + zwanzig.

strings.item.u1-q1.opt.b.why: Guten Tag je čest pozdrav, ali se kaže tek od otprilike 11 sati; do tada vrijedi Guten Morgen.
strings.item.u1-q1.opt.c.why: Učenici miješaju dobe dana; Guten Abend kaže se tek od otprilike 18 sati, a većina pozdrava ovisi o dobu dana.
strings.item.u1-q1.opt.d.why: Gute Nacht prevodi se kao 'laku noć' i kaže se kad netko ide spavati, a ne pri susretu.
strings.item.u1-q2.prompt: Napiši njemački pozdrav koji se kaže u 14 sati.
strings.item.u1-q2.expl: U 14 sati kaže se Guten Tag. Taj pozdrav vrijedi otprilike od 11 do 18 sati.
strings.item.u1-q2.hint: Podne je već prošlo, a večer još nije.
strings.item.u1-q3.expl: Od otprilike 18 sati kaže se Guten Abend, što znači 'dobra večer'.
strings.item.u1-q4.prompt: U 20 sati ulaziš u kafić. Što kažeš konobaru pri dolasku?
strings.item.u1-q4.expl: Pri dolasku u 20 sati kažeš Guten Abend. Gute Nacht nije pozdrav pri dolasku nego izraz za odlazak na spavanje.
strings.item.u1-q4.hint: Navečer dolaziš, a ne odlaziš na spavanje.
strings.item.u1-q4.opt.b.why: Hrvatski govornici 'laku noć' često koriste i za večernji pozdrav, ali Gute Nacht se kaže kad netko ide spavati, ne pri dolasku.
strings.item.u1-q4.opt.c.why: Guten Morgen vrijedi samo do otprilike 11 sati; u 20 sati je večer.
strings.item.u1-q5.prompt: Razvrstaj izraze: pozdrav pri dolasku ili izraz za odlazak na spavanje.
strings.item.u1-q5.expl: Gute Nacht kaže se kad netko ide spavati. Guten Morgen, Guten Tag i Guten Abend su pozdravi pri dolasku.
strings.item.u1-q5.dyk: Guten Abend se kaže od otprilike 18 sati.
strings.item.u1-q5.hint: Jedan izraz ne služi za pozdrav pri susretu.
strings.item.u1-q6.expl: Kad netko ide spavati, kaže se Gute Nacht, što znači 'laku noć'.
strings.item.u1-q6.hint: Zamisli da se opraštaš prije spavanja.
strings.item.u1-q7.prompt: Razgovaraš s nepoznatom starijom gospođom. Koju riječ za 'Vi' koristiš?
strings.item.u1-q7.expl: Nepoznatoj starijoj osobi obraćaš se oblikom Sie. Piše se velikim slovom S.
strings.item.u1-q7.dyk: Sie se uvijek piše velikim slovom S.
strings.item.u1-q7.hint: Nepoznata i starija osoba traži uljudan oblik.
strings.item.u1-q7.opt.b.why: Du je neformalan oblik za prijatelje, obitelj i djecu; s nepoznatom starijom osobom koristi se Sie.
strings.item.u1-q7.opt.c.why: Ihr je oblik za više osoba kojima se obraćaš s du; za uljudno obraćanje nepoznatoj osobi ne koristi se, nego Sie.
strings.item.u1-q8.prompt: S kojom osobom koristiš Sie, a s kojom du?
strings.item.u1-q8.expl: Sie koristiš s nepoznatim ljudima, u poslovnim situacijama i sa starijim osobama. Du koristiš s prijateljima, obitelji i djecom.
strings.item.u1-q8.hint: Pitaj se imaš li s osobom blizak odnos.
strings.item.u1-q9.expl: Kad nisi siguran, najsigurniji izbor je Sie. To je uljudan, formalni oblik.
strings.item.u1-q9.hint: Bolje je biti uljudan nego preblizak.
strings.item.u2-q1.expl: Glagol sein je vrlo nepravilan, baš kao engleski 'to be'. Zato oblike treba naučiti napamet: ich bin, du bist, er ist, wir sind, ihr seid.
strings.item.u2-q1.dyk: Oblik ist uvijek je jednina, a sind uvijek množina.
strings.item.u2-q1.hint: Oblici ne sliče jedan drugome, kao ni u engleskom 'am, are, is'.
strings.item.u2-q2.prompt: Koji oblik glagola sein pripada u rečenicu: Wir ___ aus Kroatien. (mi)
strings.item.u2-q2.expl: Uz wir (mi) ide oblik sind. Sind je uvijek množina, a ist je uvijek jednina.
strings.item.u2-q2.opt.b.why: Ist je oblik za jedninu (er ist). Uz wir (mi) ide množina: wir sind.
strings.item.u2-q2.opt.c.why: Seid ide uz ihr (vi, više osoba), a ne uz wir. Uz wir ide sind.
strings.item.u2-q2.opt.d.why: Bin ide samo uz ich (ja). Uz wir ide sind.
strings.item.u2-q3.expl: Uz du glagol sein glasi bist: du bist. Ne tvori se kao pravilni glagol, jer je sein vrlo nepravilan.
strings.item.u2-q4.expl: Haben je uglavnom pravilan, ali u nekim oblicima nepravilan. Zapamti du hast i er hat, a ostalo glasi ich habe, wir haben, ihr habt.
strings.item.u2-q4.hint: Dva su oblika kraća nego što bi pravilo tražilo.
strings.item.u2-q5.prompt: Koji oblik glagola haben pripada u rečenicu: Du ___ Zeit. (ti)
strings.item.u2-q5.expl: Uz du glagol haben glasi hast: du hast. Haben je u nekim oblicima nepravilan, pa se ne kaže habst.
strings.item.u2-q5.opt.b.why: Haben je djelomično nepravilan, pa se ne tvori kao pravilni glagol: du hast, a ne habst.
strings.item.u2-q5.opt.c.why: Hat ide uz er/sie/es (treće lice jednine). Uz du ide hast.
strings.item.u2-q5.opt.d.why: Habe ide uz ich (ja). Uz du ide hast.
strings.item.u2-q6.prompt: Napiši oblik glagola haben uz osobu er (bez zamjenice).
strings.item.u2-q6.expl: Uz er (on, ona, ono) glagol haben glasi hat. Završava na -t, a ne na -en.
strings.item.u2-q6.hint: Misli na oblik koji je nepravilan.
strings.item.u2-q7.prompt: Spregni pravilni glagol wohnen u prezentu.
strings.item.u2-q7.expl: Wohnen je pravilan glagol: wohne, wohnst, wohnt, wohnen, wohnt. Uljudni oblik Sie wohnen glasi kao množina, iako se može odnositi na jednu osobu.
strings.item.u2-q7.dyk: Sie se uvijek piše velikim slovom i može značiti jednu ili više osoba.
strings.item.u2-q7.hint: Slijedi isti obrazac kao singen: singe, singst, singt.
strings.item.u2-q8.prompt: Uljudno pitaš jednu nepoznatu osobu gdje stanuje: Wo ___ Sie?
strings.item.u2-q8.expl: Uz uljudno Sie glagol ima oblik na -en: Wo wohnen Sie? To vrijedi i kad pitaš samo jednu osobu.
strings.item.u2-q8.hint: Glagolski oblici na -en su množina, ali Sie je poseban.
strings.item.u2-q8.opt.b.why: Wohnt ide uz er ili ihr. Uljudni Sie uvijek traži oblik na -en: Wo wohnen Sie?
strings.item.u2-q8.opt.c.why: Wohnst ide uz du. Kad kažeš Sie, glagol je kao u množini: wohnen, iako je riječ o jednoj osobi.
strings.item.u2-q8.opt.d.why: Wohne ide uz ich (ja). Uz Sie ide wohnen.
strings.item.u2-q9.expl: Uz er glagol wohnen glasi wohnt: er wohnt. Treće lice jednine završava na -t.
strings.item.u2-q9.hint: Misli na obrazac singe, singst, singt.
strings.item.u3-q1.prompt: Kako se na njemačkom kaže broj 11?
strings.item.u3-q1.expl: Broj 11 je elf. Poslije njega dolazi zwölf, što je 12.
strings.item.u3-q2.expl: Dreißig je 30. Ne miješaj ga s dreizehn, što je 13, ni sa sechzig, što je 60.
strings.item.u3-q2.dyk: Desetice su zwanzig, dreißig, vierzig, fünfzig, sechzig, siebzig, achtzig i neunzig.
strings.item.u3-q2.hint: Desetice završavaju na -zig, a 30 se piše dreißig.
strings.item.u3-q2.opt.a.why: Dreizehn je 13, a dreißig je 30: slični su po početku, ali -zehn znači 13, a -ßig označava deseticu.
strings.item.u3-q2.opt.c.why: Drei je 3. Dreißig počinje s drei, ali je desetica: 30.
strings.item.u3-q3.expl: Poslije zehn (10) i elf (11) dolazi zwölf (12).
strings.item.u3-q4.expl: Vierzehn je 14, fünfzehn je 15, sechzehn je 16, a siebzehn je 17.
strings.item.u3-q4.hint: Prvi dio riječi je jedinica: vier, fünf, sechs, sieben.
strings.item.u3-q5.expl: U broju 24 prvo dolazi jedinica, zatim und, pa desetica: vier + und + zwanzig.
strings.item.u3-q5.dyk: Brojevi od 21 do 99 stavljaju jedinicu na prvo mjesto.
strings.item.u3-q5.opt.b.why: Redoslijed nije kao u hrvatskom ili engleskom: u njemačkom prvo ide jedinica, pa und, pa desetica.
strings.item.u3-q5.opt.c.why: Između jedinice i desetice uvijek stoji und: vier-und-zwanzig.
strings.item.u3-q5.opt.d.why: To je 42 (zwei + und + vierzig). Za 24 jedinica je vier, a desetica zwanzig.
strings.item.u3-q6.expl: Broj 21 je einundzwanzig: ein (jedan), und (i) i zwanzig (dvadeset).
strings.item.u3-q6.hint: Počinje jedinicom, a piše se u jednoj riječi.
strings.item.u3-q7.prompt: Koja riječ spaja jedinicu i deseticu u broju einundzwanzig?
strings.item.u3-q7.expl: Između jedinice i desetice stoji und, što znači 'i'. Tako nastaje ein-und-zwanzig.
strings.item.u3-q8.prompt: Kojim se redom grade njemački brojevi od 21 do 99?
strings.item.u3-q8.expl: Brojevi od 21 do 99 grade se jednako: jedinica, zatim und, pa desetica. Tako je 24 vierundzwanzig.
strings.item.u3-q8.back: Jedinica + und + desetica, na primjer vierundzwanzig (24).
strings.item.u3-q9.prompt: Konobar u kafiću te uljudno pita: "Was möchten Sie?" Što te pita?
strings.item.u3-q9.expl: Was möchten Sie? znači 'Što želite?'. Konobar tako uljudno pita što želiš naručiti.
strings.item.u3-q9.dyk: Prijatelji bi pitali: Was möchtest du?
strings.item.u3-q9.opt.b.why: Koliko to košta? je Was kostet das? Möchten pita što gost želi naručiti.
strings.item.u3-q9.opt.c.why: Kako ste? je Wie geht es Ihnen? Was möchten Sie? ne pita za zdravlje nego što želite naručiti.
strings.item.u3-q9.opt.d.why: Kako se zovete? je Wie heißen Sie? U kafiću Was möchten Sie? pita što želite.
strings.item.u3-q10.expl: Kratka narudžba glasi Einen Kaffee, bitte. Riječ bitte je uljudno 'molim'.
strings.item.u3-q10.dyk: Možeš reći i: Ich hätte gerne einen Kaffee, bitte.
strings.item.u3-q11.prompt: Čemu u kafiću služi glagol möchte?
strings.item.u3-q11.expl: Glagol möchte služi za kazivanje što netko želi naručiti. Primjer je rečenica o kolegici koja želi latte macchiato.
strings.item.u3-q11.back: Kaže se što netko želi naručiti, na primjer: meine Kollegin möchte einen Latte Macchiato.
strings.item.u4-q1.prompt: Spoji njemačku riječ s hrvatskim značenjem.
strings.item.u4-q1.expl: Der Vater je otac, die Mutter majka, das Kind dijete, a der Bruder brat. Član uči zajedno s imenicom.
strings.item.u4-q1.hint: Obrati pažnju na članove der, die i das.
strings.item.u4-q2.prompt: Napiši njemačku riječ za 'majka' zajedno s određenim članom.
strings.item.u4-q2.expl: Majka je die Mutter. Član je dio riječi, pa ga uči zajedno s imenicom.
strings.item.u4-q3.expl: Die Eltern znači roditelji, dakle majka i otac zajedno. Braća i sestre su zasebna riječ: die Geschwister.
strings.item.u4-q3.dyk: Baka i djed su die Großmutter i der Großvater, a neformalno die Oma i der Opa.
strings.item.u4-q3.opt.b.why: Die Eltern i die Geschwister se miješaju; die Geschwister znači braća i sestre, a die Eltern roditelji.
strings.item.u4-q3.opt.c.why: Djeca su die Kinder; die Eltern su oni koji imaju djecu, dakle roditelji.
strings.item.u4-q3.opt.d.why: Baka i djed su die Großmutter i der Großvater; die Eltern znači majka i otac zajedno.
strings.item.u4-q4.prompt: Napiši njemačku riječ za 'sestra' zajedno s određenim članom.
strings.item.u4-q4.expl: Sestra je die Schwester, ženskog roda. Brat je der Bruder.
strings.item.u4-q5.prompt: Koji određeni član u nominativu jednine ima imenica srednjeg roda?
strings.item.u4-q5.expl: Rod prepoznaješ po članu u nominativu jednine: der za muški, die za ženski i das za srednji rod. Primjer srednjeg roda je das Bild.
strings.item.u4-q5.hint: Tri roda, tri člana; srednji rod nije ni der ni die.
strings.item.u4-q5.opt.b.why: Der je član muškog roda (der Berg); srednji rod ima das (das Bild).
strings.item.u4-q5.opt.c.why: Die je član ženskog roda (die Kraft) i množine; srednji rod ima das.
strings.item.u4-q6.prompt: Razvrstaj imenice prema članu koji im pripada u jednini.
strings.item.u4-q6.expl: Der Berg i der Vater su muškog roda, die Kraft i die Mutter ženskog, a das Bild i das Kind srednjeg roda. Član treba učiti zajedno s imenicom.
strings.item.u4-q6.dyk: Slovo ß zove se Eszett ili scharfes S i označava dvostruko s, kao u riječi Großmutter.
strings.item.u4-q6.hint: Otac je muškog, a majka ženskog roda.
strings.item.u4-q7.expl: Njemačke imenice imaju tri roda: muški, ženski i srednji. Svaki rod ima svoj član u jednini: der, die i das.
strings.item.u4-q7.hint: Gledaj koliko članova u jednini postoji.
strings.item.u4-q7.opt.b.why: Njemački, kao i hrvatski, ima tri roda. Uz muški i ženski postoji i srednji rod, s članom das (das Kind).
strings.item.u4-q7.opt.c.why: Svaka njemačka imenica ima rod. Rod se vidi po članu der, die ili das.
strings.item.u4-q8.expl: U množini je određeni član uvijek die, za sva tri roda. Jednina je das Kind, a množina die Kinder.
strings.item.u4-q8.hint: U množini se rod više ne razlikuje.
strings.item.u4-q8.opt.b.why: Das je član jednine srednjeg roda (das Kind); u množini je član uvijek die.
strings.item.u4-q8.opt.c.why: Der je član muškog roda u jednini (der Vater); u množini svi rodovi imaju član die.
strings.item.u4-q9.expl: Der Vater je muškog roda, a die Mutter ženskog. Član uči zajedno s imenicom.
strings.item.u4-q9.hint: Otac je muškog, a majka ženskog roda.
strings.item.u4-q10.prompt: Napiši određeni član ispred riječi Eltern (roditelji, množina).
strings.item.u4-q10.expl: Die Eltern je množina, a u množini je član uvijek die. To vrijedi za sva tri roda.

strings.art.a-u1-1.title: Pozdravi i oblik obraćanja: du ili Sie
strings.art.a-u1-1.body:
Većina njemačkih pozdrava ovisi o dobu dana [1]. Zato prvo pogledaj koliko je sati: do otprilike 11 sati kaže se Guten Morgen (dobro jutro) [2], od otprilike 11 do otprilike 18 sati kaže se Guten Tag (dobar dan) [3], a navečer, od otprilike 18 sati, kaže se Guten Abend (dobra večer) [4].

Gute Nacht (laku noć) nije pozdrav pri dolasku. Kaže se kad netko ide spavati [5]. Kad navečer stigneš u goste ili u kafić, reci Guten Abend, a Gute Nacht čuvaj za odlazak na spavanje [4, 5].

Njemački ima dvije riječi za 'ti' i 'Vi': neformalno du i formalno Sie [6]. Sie se uvijek piše velikim slovom S [7].

Sie koristiš s nepoznatim ljudima, u poslovnim situacijama i sa starijim osobama [8]. Du koristiš s prijateljima, obitelji, djecom i vršnjacima kad ih već poznaješ [9]. Osnovno je pravilo: Sie kažeš osobi s kojom nemaš blizak odnos [10].

Ako nisi siguran koji oblik odabrati, najsigurniji izbor je Sie [11].
strings.art.a-u2-1.title: Glagoli sein, haben i wohnen u prezentu
strings.art.a-u2-1.body:
Glagol sein (biti) vrlo je nepravilan, baš kao engleski glagol 'to be' [1]. Njegovi oblici u prezentu glase: ich bin, du bist, er ist, wir sind, ihr seid [2]. Oblik ist uvijek je jednina, a oblik sind uvijek je množina [3].

Glagol haben (imati) ima ove oblike u prezentu: ich habe, du hast, er hat, wir haben, ihr habt [4]. Haben je uglavnom pravilan, ali u nekim oblicima nepravilan, pa ga je dobro naučiti napamet [5].

Pravilni glagoli slijede isti obrazac kao singen: singe, singst, singt, singen, singt [6]. Glagol wohnen (stanovati) sprežen je pravilno [7] i pripada vokabularu razine A1 [8]. Za treće lice jednine kažeš er wohnt [9].

U množini imamo wir wohnen i sie wohnen, a uljudni oblik glasi Sie wohnen [10]. Glagolski oblici na -en su množina, iako se uljudno Sie može odnositi na jednu osobu [11]. Sie se uvijek piše velikim slovom i koristi se za jednu osobu i za više osoba [12].
strings.art.a-u3-1.title: Brojevi i naručivanje u kafiću
strings.art.a-u3-1.body:
Njemački brojevi od 0 do 20 temelj su za sve ostale njemačke brojeve [1]. Zato ih prvo dobro nauči. Brojevi od 0 do 12 su: null, eins, zwei, drei, vier, fünf, sechs, sieben, acht, neun, zehn, elf i zwölf [2].

Brojevi od 13 do 19 su: dreizehn, vierzehn, fünfzehn, sechzehn, siebzehn, achtzehn i neunzehn [3]. Desetice su: zwanzig (20), dreißig (30), vierzig (40), fünfzig (50), sechzig (60), siebzig (70), achtzig (80) i neunzig (90) [4].

Brojevi od 21 do 99 grade se po jednom pravilu. Prvo dolazi jedinica, zatim und ("i"), a na kraju desetica, pa je 24 vierundzwanzig [5]. Tako je 21 einundzwanzig: ein (jedan), und (i) i zwanzig (dvadeset) [6].

U njemačkom kafiću konobar pita gosta što želi. Uljudno pitanje je "Was möchten Sie?", a među prijateljima kaže se "Was möchtest du?" [7]. Glagolom möchte kažeš što netko želi naručiti [8].

Narudžba može biti kratka: "Einen Kaffee, bitte." [9]. Možeš reći i "Ich hätte gerne einen Kaffee, bitte" ili "Ich nehme einen Espresso" [10].
strings.art.a-u4-1.title: Obitelj i tri roda imenica
strings.art.a-u4-1.body:
Njemačke imenice imaju tri roda: muški, ženski i srednji [1]. Rod prepoznaješ po određenom članu u nominativu jednine: der za muški, die za ženski i das za srednji rod [2]. Primjeri su der Berg (muški), die Kraft (ženski) i das Bild (srednji) [3].

U množini je određeni član u nominativu uvijek die, za sva tri roda [4]. Zato član uči zajedno s imenicom: ne uči Vater, nego der Vater.

Riječ za obitelj je die Familie [5]. Otac, majka i dijete su der Vater, die Mutter i das Kind [6]. Sin, kći, brat i sestra su der Sohn, die Tochter, der Bruder i die Schwester [7].

Die Eltern znači roditelji, a die Geschwister znači braća i sestre [8]. Baka i djed su die Großmutter i der Großvater, a neformalno die Oma i der Opa [9]. Der Onkel je stric ili ujak, a die Tante je teta [10].

Uoči slovo ß u riječi Großmutter. Zove se Eszett ili scharfes S i označava dvostruko s [11].
strings.fact.f1.claim: German speakers say Guten Morgen (good morning) until about 11 AM.
strings.fact.f2.claim: German speakers say Guten Tag (good day, hello) from about 11 AM to about 6 PM.
strings.fact.f3.claim: German speakers say Guten Abend (good evening) in the evening, from about 6 PM.
strings.fact.f4.claim: Gute Nacht (good night) is said when someone is going to bed, not as a greeting on arrival.
strings.fact.f5.claim: German has two words for 'you': the formal Sie and the informal du.
strings.fact.f6.claim: The formal Sie is always written with a capital S.
strings.fact.f7.claim: German speakers use Sie with strangers, in professional settings and with older people.
strings.fact.f8.claim: German speakers use du with friends, family, children and people of their own age once they know them.
strings.fact.f9.claim: When a learner is unsure whether to use du or Sie, the safe choice is Sie.
strings.fact.f10.claim: The basic rule is to use Sie with a person you do not have a close relationship with.
strings.fact.f11.claim: Most German greetings depend on the time of day.
strings.fact.f12.claim: The German verb wohnen (to live, to reside) is conjugated regularly.
strings.fact.f13.claim: The verb wohnen belongs to the A1 level vocabulary of German.
strings.fact.f14.claim: The third person singular present form of wohnen is wohnt (er wohnt).
strings.fact.f15.claim: In the present tense the plural forms of wohnen are wir wohnen and sie wohnen, and the formal form is Sie wohnen.
strings.fact.f16.claim: The verb sein (to be) is highly irregular, like the English verb 'to be'.
strings.fact.f17.claim: The present tense forms of sein are bin, bist, ist, sind and seid (ich bin, du bist, er ist, wir sind, ihr seid).
strings.fact.f18.claim: The form ist of sein is always singular and the form sind is always plural.
strings.fact.f19.claim: The present tense forms of haben (to have) are habe, hast, hat, haben and habt (ich habe, du hast, er hat, wir haben, ihr habt).
strings.fact.f20.claim: The verb haben is mostly weak but irregular in some forms.
strings.fact.f21.claim: A regular German present tense follows the pattern of singen: singe, singst, singt, singen, singt.
strings.fact.f22.claim: German verb forms ending in -en are plural, although the formal Sie can refer to one person.
strings.fact.f23.claim: The formal Sie is always capitalised and is used for both one person and several people.
strings.fact.f24.claim: German nouns have three grammatical genders: masculine, feminine and neuter.
strings.fact.f25.claim: The definite article in the nominative singular is der for masculine nouns, die for feminine nouns and das for neuter nouns.
strings.fact.f26.claim: Examples of the three genders are der Berg (masculine), die Kraft (feminine) and das Bild (neuter).
strings.fact.f27.claim: In the nominative plural the definite article is die for all three genders.
strings.fact.f28.claim: The German words for father, mother and child are der Vater, die Mutter and das Kind.
strings.fact.f29.claim: The German words for son, daughter, brother and sister are der Sohn, die Tochter, der Bruder and die Schwester.
strings.fact.f30.claim: Die Eltern means the parents and die Geschwister means the brothers and sisters.
strings.fact.f31.claim: The German words for grandmother and grandfather are die Großmutter and der Großvater, informally die Oma and der Opa.
strings.fact.f32.claim: The German words for uncle and aunt are der Onkel and die Tante.
strings.fact.f33.claim: The German word for family is die Familie.
strings.fact.f34.claim: The German letter ß, called Eszett or scharfes S, stands for a double s, as in Großmutter.
strings.fact.f35.claim: The German numbers from 0 to 20 are the basis for all other German numbers.
strings.fact.f36.claim: The German word for 21 is einundzwanzig: ein (one) plus und (and) plus zwanzig (twenty).
strings.fact.f37.claim: German numbers from 21 to 99 put the ones digit first, then und, then the tens, so 24 is vierundzwanzig.
strings.fact.f38.claim: The German numbers from 0 to 12 are null, eins, zwei, drei, vier, fünf, sechs, sieben, acht, neun, zehn, elf and zwölf.
strings.fact.f39.claim: The German numbers from 13 to 19 are dreizehn, vierzehn, fünfzehn, sechzehn, siebzehn, achtzehn and neunzehn.
strings.fact.f40.claim: The German tens are zwanzig (20), dreißig (30), vierzig (40), fünfzig (50), sechzig (60), siebzig (70), achtzig (80) and neunzig (90).
strings.fact.f41.claim: In a German cafe a customer can order with 'Einen Kaffee, bitte.'
strings.fact.f42.claim: In a German cafe a customer can order with 'Ich hätte gerne einen Kaffee, bitte' or 'Ich nehme einen Espresso'.
strings.fact.f43.claim: German cafe staff ask 'Was möchten Sie?' (formal) or 'Was möchtest du?' (informal) to ask what a customer wants.
strings.fact.f44.claim: The verb möchte is used to say what someone wants to order, as in 'meine Kollegin möchte einen Latte Macchiato'.
strings.fact.f45.claim: In German 10 is zehn, 11 is elf and 12 is zwölf.
strings.fact.f46.claim: In German 14 is vierzehn, 15 is fünfzehn, 16 is sechzehn and 17 is siebzehn.
strings.fact.f47.claim: The page on German numbers from 1 to 100 lists 29 basic number words to learn.
strings.rp.sc.u1-hotel.title: Dolazak u hotel
strings.rp.sc.u1-hotel.setting: Hotel Linde, 20 sati. Stižeš u hotel i recepcionarka gospođa Weber te dočekuje. Cilj: pozdraviti prema dobu dana i razgovarati s nepoznatom osobom formalno, sa Sie.
strings.rp.sc.u1-hotel.l2.help: Sada je 20 sati, večer. Pozdravi gospođu Weber pozdravom koji se kaže navečer.
strings.rp.sc.u1-hotel.l3.tr: Ja sam gospođa Weber. Drago mi je! Izvolite vaš ključ.
strings.rp.sc.u1-hotel.l4.help: Gospođa Weber je nepoznata osoba na poslu. Pitaj je kako je, ali formalno: s Ihnen, a ne s dir.
strings.rp.sc.u1-hotel.l6.help: Ideš u sobu spavati. To nije pozdrav za dolazak kao Guten Abend: što se kaže kad netko ide spavati?
strings.rp.sc.u1-hotel.l8.tr: (Sljedeće jutro.) Osam je sati. Doručak je spreman!
strings.rp.sc.u1-hotel.l9.help: Sada je 8 sati ujutro. Napiši pozdrav koji se kaže do otprilike 11 sati: Guten ...
strings.rp.sc.u2-sprachcafe.title: U jezičnom kafiću
strings.rp.sc.u2-sprachcafe.setting: Berlin, jezični kafić za ljude koji uče njemački. Upoznaješ Pabla iz Španjolske. Cilj: reći odakle dolaziš, gdje stanuješ i imaš li vremena za zajedničko učenje.
strings.rp.sc.u2-sprachcafe.l1.tr: Bok! Ja sam Pablo. Dolazim iz Španjolske. Učim njemački.
strings.rp.sc.u2-sprachcafe.l3.help: Pablo pita odakle dolaziš. Odgovori za sebe: glagol kommen uz ich završava na -e, a zemlja dolazi poslije aus.
strings.rp.sc.u2-sprachcafe.l4.tr: Iz Hrvatske? Hrvatska je lijepa zemlja! A gdje stanuješ?
strings.rp.sc.u2-sprachcafe.l5.help: Pablo pita gdje stanuješ. Počni s Ich i glagolom wohnen u obliku za ich, pa dodaj in Zagreb.
strings.rp.sc.u2-sprachcafe.l6.tr: Zagreb je lijep grad! A tvoj prijatelj Marko? Je li i on ovdje u Berlinu?
strings.rp.sc.u2-sprachcafe.l7.help: Marko nije u Berlinu. Reci da on stanuje u Zagrebu: glagol wohnen uz er završava na -t.
strings.rp.sc.u2-sprachcafe.l8.tr: Učimo zajedno njemački, može? Imaš li danas vremena?
strings.rp.sc.u2-sprachcafe.l9.help: Pablo pita imaš li danas vremena. Odgovori za sebe, osoba ich: glagol haben uz ich završava na -e.
strings.rp.sc.u3-cafe.title: U kafiću
strings.rp.sc.u3-cafe.setting: Kafić u Beču, poslijepodne. Konobar Jonas te poslužuje. Cilj: ljubazno naručiti kavu i kolač, pitati cijenu i platiti račun.
strings.rp.sc.u3-cafe.l1.tr: Dobar dan! Imamo kavu, čaj i kolače. Što želite?
strings.rp.sc.u3-cafe.l2.help: Jonas pita što želiš. Naruči kavu i dodaj ljubaznu riječ koja znači 'molim'.
strings.rp.sc.u3-cafe.l3.tr: Rado. A komad kolača? Kolač je danas jako dobar.
strings.rp.sc.u3-cafe.l4.help: Želiš znati koliko kolač košta. Postavi pitanje o cijeni.
strings.rp.sc.u3-cafe.l6.help: Jonas čeka narudžbu. Reci ljubazno da želiš komad kolača: Ich möchte ... i na kraju riječ za 'molim'.
strings.rp.sc.u3-cafe.l7.tr: Izvolite! Evo vaše kave, vašeg kolača i vode.
strings.rp.sc.u3-cafe.l8.tr: A ovo je račun. (Na računu piše 11 €.)
strings.rp.sc.u3-cafe.l9.help: Na računu piše 11 €. Reci iznos na njemačkom: koja riječ znači 11?
strings.rp.sc.u4-foto.title: Obiteljska fotografija
strings.rp.sc.u4-foto.setting: Kod prijateljice Mije doma. Mia ti pokazuje fotografiju svoje obitelji. Cilj: imenovati članove obitelji s pravim članom i reći nešto o svojoj obitelji.
strings.rp.sc.u4-foto.l1.tr: Pogledaj! Ovo je moja obitelj. Pogodi: tko je ovo?
strings.rp.sc.u4-foto.l2.help: Mia pokazuje oca i majku. Vater je muškog roda, a Mutter ženskog: koji član ide uz svaku riječ?
strings.rp.sc.u4-foto.l3.tr: Točno! A ovo je moj brat Paul. Ima trideset godina.
strings.rp.sc.u4-foto.l5.help: Mia pita imaš li braće ili sestara. Reci da imaš jednu sestru: počni s Ja, ich habe ... i ne zaboravi da je Schwester ženskog roda.
strings.rp.sc.u4-foto.l6.tr: Lijepo! A tvoji roditelji? Gdje oni stanuju?
strings.rp.sc.u4-foto.l7.help: Mia pita gdje stanuju tvoji roditelji. Eltern je množina: trebaš meine i glagol u množini.
strings.rp.sc.u4-foto.l8.tr: Super! Paul ima dvoje djece: Lenu i Maxa.
strings.rp.sc.u4-foto.l9.help: Kinder je množina od Kind. U množini svi rodovi imaju isti član: koji?
strings.rp.sc.u4-foto.l10.tr: Da, jako slatki! A ovdje su moja baka i moj djed.
strings.rp.sc.finale.title: Mijin rođendan
strings.rp.sc.finale.setting: Berlin, 19 sati, Mijin rođendan kod nje doma. Upoznaješ njezina brata Paula i njegovu kćer. Cilj: pozdraviti, reći odakle si i gdje stanuješ, ljubazno uzeti kolač i pogoditi koliko Mia ima godina.
strings.rp.sc.finale.l2.help: Sada je 19 sati, večer. Pozdravi Miju pozdravom za večer: Guten ...
strings.rp.sc.finale.l4.tr: Bok! Drago mi je. Odakle si?
strings.rp.sc.finale.l5.help: Paul pita odakle dolaziš. Glagol kommen uz ich završava na -e, a zemlja dolazi poslije aus.
strings.rp.sc.finale.l6.tr: Super! Stanuješ li ovdje u Berlinu?
strings.rp.sc.finale.l7.help: Paul pita stanuješ li u Berlinu. Ne stanuješ: reci da stanuješ u Zagrebu, glagol wohnen uz ich.
strings.rp.sc.finale.l8.tr: Evo moje rođendanske torte! Želiš li komad?
strings.rp.sc.finale.l9.help: Mia ti nudi tortu. Reci ljubazno da želiš komad: Ich möchte ... i na kraju riječ za 'molim'.
strings.rp.sc.finale.l10.tr: A ovo je moja kći Lena. Ima četiri godine.
strings.rp.sc.finale.l11.help: Kind je imenica srednjeg roda. Koji član ide uz srednji rod: der, die ili das?
strings.rp.sc.finale.l12.tr: Pogodi: koliko danas imam godina? Dvadeset plus jedan!
strings.rp.sc.finale.l13.help: Dvadeset plus jedan je 21. Na njemačkom prvo ide jedinica, pa und, pa desetica: ein + und + zwanzig.
